key_insight: EnerGNN learns energy functions over binary configurations that can be minimized exactly under explicit hard constraints using mixed integer programming.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports feasible combinatorial decisions and zero-shot constraint changes without retraining, making it relevant to adaptive engineering planning.
method: Encode problem instances with a graph neural network.
Combine an optimization-compatible readout with a nonlinear energy head.
Train with an optimality-aware contrastive loss, then minimize learned energy under hard constraints using MIP.
evidence_signal: Across Quadratic Knapsack, Combinatorial Auctions, and personalized cell therapy supply chain evaluations, EnerGNN reports near-optimal solutions with 100% feasibility; the supply chain task achieves a 0.05% mean primal gap and 17.4× speedup over monolithic MIP.
watch_item: Exact minimization of the learned energy does not guarantee optimality for the original objective, and MIP runtime may remain a scaling bottleneck.
paper_title: EnerGNN: Learning Optimization-Compatible Energy Functions for Exact Constrained Combinatorial Inference
